title: Hierarchical charge scorer for per-route/model/customer attribution
creator: Maya Iqbal
description: Build a deterministic, explainable scoring layer that computes a hierarchical breakdown of inference cost and latency across route -> model -> customer dimensions. The service will consume runtime telemetry and billing signals to produce a scored attribution tree that powers Console breakdowns, cost alerts, and per-tenant charge estimates.
goal: Replace the brittle ad-hoc apportioner with a streaming scorer that (1) attributes cost and latency at multiple granularities, (2) exposes uncertainty scores and dominant contributors, and (3) supports deterministic offline recompute for audits.
background: Current console views aggregate cost and latency using heuristics that diverge when retries, fallbacks, or mixed-model routing occur. Engineers and customers have asked for more explainability and a clear path to reconcile discrepancies between billing and telemetry. This ticket defines the scorer algorithm and implements the core streaming service.
data_pipelines: Ingest: Kafka topics runtime-telemetry, token-ledger, model-variants (partitioned by tenant_id)
Enrichment: Join telemetry with token-ledger using event_id and time-window, correct for retry inflation and batching artifacts
Compute: Flink job that maintains per-route/model/customer state with sliding windows and hierarchical rollups
Materialization: Write per-minute scored snapshots to ClickHouse 'econ_snapshots' and per-entity time-series to TimescaleDB for console charts
algorithm_overview: Score composition: score = base_token_cost + batch_overhead + kv_cache_delta
Hierarchical allocation: compute leaf-level raw costs, then propagate up with weight adjustments for shared resources and fallback models
Uncertainty model: each allocation includes a variance estimate derived from sampling and trace coverage; shown as an uncertainty score in UI
Debiasing rules: subtract traced retry tokens, attribute retries to initiating route unless retry caused by fallback policy
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline processes synthetic load and produces per-route/model/customer snapshots within 4 minutes of event ingestion
Console breakdown UI shows explanation panel with dominant contributors and uncertainty score
Recompute mode: given the same telemetry snapshot, offline recompute produces identical results to streaming scorer
Unit tests cover edge cases: model fallbacks, multi-tenant batching, zero-token responses, and KV cache hits
Benchmark: scorer CPU + memory fits a single m5-like worker for 10k routes with <5s compute latency per minute window
work_log: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on hierarchical tree shape and that scoring must be deterministic. Action: Maya to produce first draft of composition rules.
2025-02-18: Prototype Flink pipeline ingests sample telemetry. Initial join stability OK but discovered 1.5x token inflation from retries.
2025-02-22: Decision: attribute retry tokens to original route unless HTTP 5xx from model, in which case fallback model bears cost. Documented rule in design doc.
2025-02-26: Implemented uncertainty estimator using reservoir sampling of traces (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1872).
2025-03-01: Integration tests running in staging; noted schema mismatch between runtime-telemetry v2 and token-ledger; assigned schema migration to ENG-942001.
engineering_notes: State management: store per-tenant hierarchies keyed by (tenant, minute) and use compacted changelog topic for recovery
Hot keys: shard by tenant_id with range partitioning; provide backpressure if a tenant exceeds memory budget
Determinism: use event-time processing with bounded out-of-order window (120s), and canonical tie-breaker by event_id
Performance: pre-aggregate at router edge for common routes to reduce join cardinality
Observability: emit explainability traces with top-3 contributors and confidence per snapshot
qa_plan: Synthetic workloads that exercise fallback chains, 0-token responses, and KV cache hit/miss patterns
Golden dataset produced offline and stored in S3 to verify streaming vs offline parity
Canary rollout: enable scorer-derived breakdown for 10% of Console requests and compare against existing apportioner for 48h
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy scorer job in staging, backfill 72h of telemetry, validate parity
Phase 2: Canary in production for 10% tenants with feature flag and discrepancy alerting
Phase 3: Full flip with guardrail disabling if discrepancy > 5% for any top-level route
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High-cardinality tenants could blow memory. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant window cap and evict least-recently-updated routes
Risk: Schema drift on runtime telemetry. Mitigation: validation layer that drops nonconforming messages to dead-letter topic and alerts
Risk: Customer-facing mismatch with billing. Mitigation: provide audit mode and offline recompute for dispute resolution
